reason: The cited evidence does not address FeMnNiGeSi alloys, thin films, or strain effects on magnetocaloric response. E1 discusses a different material system (perovskite manganites) and notes reduced MCE in nanocrystalline samples, which contradicts the premise that annealing improves MCE. E2 describes domain wall pinning at grain/twin boundaries in HEAs but does not link this to residual strain, annealing, or magnetocaloric properties. The key premises thus lack specific prior support.
premises: Residual strain in thin films increases domain wall pinning and hysteresis
Thermal annealing relaxes strain and reduces defect density
Reduced pinning lowers coercivity and narrows hysteresis
Narrower hysteresis enhances reversible magnetocaloric entropy change
These mechanisms apply to FeMnNiGeSi-type high-entropy alloys
